text:
elena: Heads-up — saw a 2.3x token-level latency spike on a customer Private VPC yesterday around 03:22UTC. Correlated with a kernel-selection roll (auto) + a KV cache miss surge. Can folks weigh in?

matt: ugh. which customer / route?

elena: acme-inc, route_id=nlp-search-prod. Metric: token_latency_ms_bucket and token_generation_phase{phase=\"kv_read\"} showed big tail. Happened right after we pushed kernel-decider v2 (commit abc123).

jia: I pulled traces. The runtime switched from kernel=mtx_opt to kernel=fallback in ~70% of inferences due to sequence-length histogram mismatch. KV miss rate jumped from 4% -> 28%.

priya: are they on airgapped export? means we can't query their prometheus directly. We only get periodic tarball pushes.

elena: yes private deployment with prometheus-exporter-shipper (airgap mode). They only upload bundles every 30m. The spike window shows within one bundle.

matt: what do dashboards show? any per-route breakdown panel?

elena: their Grafana has our shipped dashboard but missing token_phase histogram panel. We had token_phase instrumented but not wired into the default dashboard.

tom: quick ask: can we get the exact promql for the interesting series?

jia: paste: ```
# 95th pct token latency per route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, route_id))

# KV miss rate per route
sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (route_id) /
(sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) by (route_id) + sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (route_id))
```

matt: thanks. Also add label kernel and model_variant to token_latency_ms buckets. That'll let us slice by kernel-decider choice.

elena: agreed. I noticed our kernel selector added heuristic: \"prefer_mt_size\". It didn't consider cached_kv_prefixes. So for some long-tail prompts it picked slower kernels that don't overlap well with KV layout.

priya: for airgapped customers we should enhance the exporter to include per-token-phase counters and kernel_label. That way their offline Grafana can alert.

infra-bot: deploy queued: revert candidate abc123 -> rolling canary disabled. ETA 12m.

matt: good temporary rollback. Long term: add a metric token_generation_phase_duration_ms with labels {route_id, kernel, phase}. Histogram with explicit buckets [0.1,1,2,5,10,20,50,100,200,500].

jia: also we'll add a diagnostic trace sampler that records KV key counts fetched per request. Sample rate 1/200 for now.

elena: created a quick dashboard patch for airgapped teams: panels: \"Token latency by kernel\", \"KV miss rate heatmap\", \"Per-route 95th vs baseline\". sketch here: https://go/rw-dash/patch-priv-1969 (internal link).

priya: exporter changes for airgap: include a small metadata file with commit id + promql snippets we recommend. Then our solutions team can drop into customer's Grafana.

tom: for immediate triage, can we add an alert: if kv_cache_miss_rate > 15% and fraction(kernel=fallback) > 0.5 for 3m then fire pager? For now send to perf-oncall channel.

elena: I'll add the alert in our internal default rule set (not pushed to customer) and also add recommended alert text for customers.

matt: action items
- elena: add kernel label to token latency histograms and push patch (due EOD)
- jia: add diagnostic KV sampler + small op-trace (PR by tomorrow)
- priya: update airgap exporter to include metrics + metadata snippets (Weds)
- tom: add pager alert + runbook (today)

priya: question: for airgap export format we currently tar gz everything and customer rsync's it out. Should we include a pushgateway shim so customers can push metrics in near-realtime to our ingest proxy when allowed?

matt: pushgateway for private deployments is risky (security) but a push-shim that writes to local prometheus push endpoint and then the shipper includes those scraped metrics could work. Documented opt-in.

jia: also flag: once we switch to kernel labels we'll have high cardinality. Use route_id and kernel only; avoid model revision and prompt_id. Also set metric cardinality cap via relabeling in exporter.

elena: noted. final note: the perf regression is likely combo of kernel-decider heuristic + KV coldset. Reverting kernel change should reduce the tail while we roll the longer-term fixes.

ops-bot: rollback completed at 03:35UTC (deploy abc123 -> abc122). Canary disabled.

tom: great. I'll monitor dashboards for the next 2 hours. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

elena: thanks team. I'll file a short postmortem if we see recurrence.
